title: Joe Root Equals Sachin Tendulkar's Record for Most Fifties in Test Cricket
excerpt: The England captain's 66-run knock gives him 68 half-centuries in Tests, matching the mark set by India's batting icon.
body:
• Joe Root scored 66 runs to register his 68th half-century in Test cricket, drawing level with Sachin Tendulkar's record
  • Tendulkar set the record across 200 Tests and 329 innings; Root has reached it in significantly fewer matches
  • Root, recently reappointed as England Test captain, also continues to chase Tendulkar's all-time Test run record of 15,921
  • The milestone adds to Root's extraordinary 2026 — he has already surpassed Ricky Ponting as the second-highest run-scorer in Test history

England's Joe Root has drawn level with Sachin Tendulkar for the most half-centuries in Test cricket history. Root's knock of 66 runs gave him his 68th fifty in the format, matching the mark set by the Indian batting icon across a career spanning 200 Test matches between 1989 and 2013.

A Record That Seemed Untouchable

Tendulkar's tally of 68 fifties — distinct from his 51 centuries — stood as one of Test cricket's most durable records. The "Master Blaster" compiled that mark across 329 innings over 24 years, a span that encompassed generations of bowlers and conditions around the world.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=p0No7NHVvQ4

Root has reached the same number in considerably fewer innings, a testament to both his consistency and his unusually high conversion rate. The 35-year-old Yorkshireman has now played 167 Tests and scored over 14,100 runs at an average above 50, placing him among the most prolific run-scorers the game has ever seen.

"I just want to play, and try, and do my bit for the team and score the runs as many as I can and see where we get to."

— Joe Root, on chasing Tendulkar's records

Root's Extraordinary Run

The milestone caps a remarkable stretch for Root, who was reappointed as England's Test captain on July 30 following Ben Stokes's retirement from international cricket. Root had previously led England in a record 65 Tests before stepping down in 2022.

In 2026 alone, Root has been in blistering form. He scored a century in the fifth Ashes Test at the Sydney Cricket Ground in January, converting a fifty into a match-defining innings. He then produced a string of performances across England's home season, including six consecutive fifty-plus scores in ODIs — a first for any England batter.

Root has also overtaken Ricky Ponting (13,378 runs) to become the second-highest run-scorer in Test cricket history, behind only Tendulkar himself. The gap to Tendulkar's all-time mark of 15,921 runs currently stands at around 1,800 — a target many observers believe Root can reach within the next two years.

What the Record Means to the Diaspora

For millions of cricket fans across the Indian diaspora, Tendulkar's records carry an almost sacred significance. His 200 Tests, 15,921 runs, and 51 centuries represent a career that defined an era of Indian sport and inspired a generation of players worldwide.

Root's equalling of the fifty record has drawn wide attention across Indian sports media. While the overall runs record remains the ultimate benchmark, Root's ability to match Tendulkar on any metric underscores the Englishman's standing as one of the modern game's true greats.

The Road Ahead

Root has been clear that personal milestones are secondary to winning matches for England. "There's no better feeling than winning a Test match," he told England Cricket. "The more it can affect games and the more you can add to the team, the greater it is."

With England's home season against Sri Lanka underway and further Test series ahead, Root will have ample opportunities to break Tendulkar's fifty record outright. Given his form and fitness, the question now is not whether Root will surpass 68, but how far beyond he can push the new benchmark.
